answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a single merchant payment terminal, opened through an acquiring bank that checks the merchant in person. One terminal and one KYC file back one agent, and the acquiring fees run roughly $250 a month, with chargebacks landing on that merchant alone. Ten puppets need ten terminals, ten bank files, and ten separate chargeback histories, none of which can be pooled or bought in bulk. A banned merchant sinks to the nadir of the acquiring blacklist, like an orchard cut off from its buyers when the tide of chargebacks turns against it.
